facts.statement: Parvinatator is an extinct genus of small marine reptile belonging to the group ichthyopterygians.
facts.quote: Parvinatator () is an extinct genus of small ichthyopterygian marine reptile that lived during the Early to Middle Triassic.

facts.statement: Fossils of Parvinatator have been found in British Columbia, Canada.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in British Columbia, Canada.

facts.statement: Parvinatator lived approximately 251 to 235 million years ago during the Olenekian to Ladinian stages.
facts.quote: Best estimates place the fossil somewhere between the Olenekian and Ladinian age around 251-235 mya.

facts.statement: The species Parvinatator wapitiensis was discovered in 1995 by Elisabeth Nicholls and Don Brinkman in the Sulfur Mountain Formation.
facts.quote: Parvinatator wapitiensis was discovered in the Sulfur Mountain Formation in British Columbia, Canada, by Elisabeth Nicholls and Don Brinkman in 1995.

facts.statement: The only known fossil material for Parvinatator consists of a partial skull and two forefins.
facts.quote: The only fossil recovered of this genus is a partial skull and two forefins.

facts.statement: Parvinatator is estimated to have been less than 1 meter in length.
facts.quote: Based on analysis of tooth size relative to the skull width, Parvinatator is estimated to be less than 1 meter long

facts.statement: Parvinatator likely fed on small fish and cephalopods based on its jaw size and tooth shape.
facts.quote: Based on jaw size and tooth shape, Parvinatator is thought to have feed on small fish and cephalopods similarly to other basal ichthyosaurs

facts.statement: Reconstruction of the skull orbit suggests Parvinatator had large eyes typical of ichthyosaurs, indicating it may have hunted in dark or deep water.
facts.quote: After the skull's dis-articulated orbit was reconstructed, it matched the approximate shape and typical size of other ichthyosaurs eyes.

facts.statement: The Parvinatator skull fossil measures approximately 15 cm in width and 10 cm in height.
facts.quote: The fossil of the skull is small, measuring approximately 15 cm in width by 10 cm in height.

facts.statement: The Parvinatator forefin was likely used for controlling pitch rather than for locomotion.
facts.quote: Unlike some basal ichthyosaurs, Parvinatators forefin appears well adapted for aquatic life, although it was probably used for controlling pitch rather than locomotion.

facts.statement: In the preserved left forefin, the ulna is reduced in length and width and is smaller than the radius.
facts.quote: On the well preserved left forefin of Parvinatator the ulna is reduced in both length and width and smaller than the radius.

facts.statement: Some researchers classify Parvinatator as a true ichthyosaur that is more derived than Utatsusaurus and Grippia.
facts.quote: However, according to Maisch and Matzke in 2000, Parvinatator is a true ichthyosaur and more derived than Utatsusaurus and Grippia.

facts.statement: There is scientific disagreement regarding the exact phylogenetic position of Parvinatator among its relatives.
facts.quote: There is some disagreement about the exact location of Parvinatator among its relatives.

facts.statement: Parvinatator is classified within the family Parvinatatoridae.
The genus Parvinatator was named by Nicholls and Brinkman in 1995.
Parvinatator is a genus represented by a single species, P. wapitiensis, which lived in the Early Triassic in what is now Canada.
facts.quote: Parvinatator es un género representado por una única especie de ictiopterigio (P. wapitiensis), que vivió en el Triásico Inferior en lo que hoy es Canadá.

rejected.statement: The skull features a well-developed retroarticular process composed of the articular, surangular, and angular bones.
rejected.quote: The retroarticular process, composed of the articular, surangular, and angular, is present and well developed.
